item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief: Implement `retry_budget.py` in the repository according to `SPEC.md` at the repository root. Preserve the documented API exactly. Handle every error and boundary case the spec describes. Add focused tests covering those cases; the existing tests cover basics only, so extend them rather than replacing them. Use only the Python standard library. Run the test suite and confirm it passes. Commit the work on the item's branch with a clear commit message. Do not push. Do not add attribution lines to the commit. Follow the repository's coding conventions: functions under 60 lines, meaningful assertions at boundaries, no silent failure handling, and no unnecessary comments.

model_reasons.implement: Small self-contained stdlib module with a written spec; medium effort suffices.

pr.body: Approach: retry_delay validates all arguments first (int only, bool and float rejected, minimums enforced), then applies the attempt-limit check, computes min(cap_ms, base_ms * 2**(attempt-1)) via _backoff with shortcuts for zero base/cap, base >= cap, and shift >= cap.bit_length() so no large power of two is built, applies retry_after_ms as a floor, and refuses when elapsed_ms + delay >= budget_ms. Key files: retry_budget.py, test_retry_budget.py. Checks: python3 -m unittest -v, 28 tests OK; py_compile OK. pyflakes not available. Assumptions: the existing 3 tests are kept unchanged. Follow-up: add bool/float rejection tests for budget_ms and cap_ms keywords (reviewer, non-blocking).

evidence.caption: Test run before the change (stub in place): 3 existing tests error with NotImplementedError

pr.summary: Made retry scheduling exist: retry_delay returns the wait before the next attempt, or None. Now: strict input validation, attempt limit, capped exponential backoff, Retry-After floor, and budget refusal. Before: stub raising NotImplementedError; now: 28 passing tests.
pr.title: Implement retry_delay per SPEC.md with validation and tests

risk.why: New isolated pure module with no callers, no I/O, no shared state. Behaviour is covered by 28 tests; the reviewer checked each SPEC rule and found no defects, and assessed the risk as low.
